package.packaging_note: Scripts/package_mac.sh reported Error_UnknownCookFailure after the cook had finished (LogCook: Done!). The cause is the Aura editor plugin: with it enabled the run logs a LogGameFeatures error about a missing AssetManager rule for GameFeatureData, and a commandlet exits non-zero when its error summary is non-empty. 129 packaged only because the editor had Aura disabled in the working tree at that moment. 130 was packaged with Aura disabled and the .uproject restored to true afterwards; the plugin is TargetAllowList Editor-only, so it is not in the shipped app either way.

the_picnic_pose.why_it_was_wrong: Three earlier attempts applied the hip pitch in bone space. This crowd rig's bone axes are not the actor's axes, so the femur swung out of the sagittal plane - legs through the cloth, knees in the air, and finally a standing pair nobody asked for. Build 129 stopped them lying and stood them up, which is not a picnic.
fix: Limb rotations are built in component space about the actor's own axes (BoneSpace = ParentComp^-1 * D * ParentComp * BoneSpace).
AimBone turns a limb onto an absolute world direction with FQuat::FindBetweenNormals, so the idle clip's pose does not matter.
The torso yaw is measured once from the shoulder bones, because the rig's rest yaw is not the actor's yaw; without it the legs pointed one way and the chest faced another.
The body is dropped until the lowest sampled leg point (minus a per-bone radius) sits on the measured cloth height.
the_picnic_pose.bug_found_on_the_way: The 'cloth height was set' test was PicnicClothZ > 0, and the park sits at a negative world Z, so every chiller fell back to ground height and sat ~21 cm into the grass and cloth. It is an explicit flag now.

drone_audit.problem: BattleDroneAudit stage 7 failed on the Mac sweep (off_target_cm 2830.6, aim_off_deg 0.00, drone health untouched) and on the Windows packaged build (2827.2). Two platforms, the same number, so it was never a platform difference.
drone_audit.cause: The eye the shot starts from is on a 3.2 m spring arm, so under load it is not the eye the stage-5 clearance sweep measured. Retrying the shot - which HEAD already did three times - cannot fix a line that runs into scenery; the line has to be re-made.
fix: Before firing, the audit re-checks the sightline the shot will actually take, from the eye it will actually start at, ignoring the drone itself.
If that line is blocked it re-places the drone on a clear bearing, bounded to three attempts so a genuinely blocked world still fails the audit.
The failure line now names the blocker (eye, view, shot_end, cam_block, at_cm, muzzle) instead of leaving four causes indistinguishable.
drone_audit.evidence: BattleDroneAudit green in the 28-audit sweep and in three standalone runs
